title: Add guided RAG unified-tool-matrix quickstart
author: Asha Nair
release_notes: Introduces a guided quickstart that demonstrates composing multiple tool bindings and split-index retrieval patterns with integrated telemetry presets.
summary: New quickstart that demonstrates composing tool-calling patterns with split-index retrieval and telemetry probes for production-like RAG workflows.
body: Motivation | This quickstart was created to give engineers a compact, opinionated example for building a RAG pipeline that calls multiple external tools (search, calendar, sheets) and uses a split-index retrieval strategy (short-term dense index + long-term sparse index) with adaptive routing and telemetry hooks. The motivating use-case was a customer ask to show how to: 1) route retrieval queries between a high-recall sparse index and a low-latency dense index, 2) surface tool-call traces for debugging, and 3) keep example infrastructure minimal for local runs. What this PR adds | A brand-new quickstart directory quickstarts/unified-tool-matrix with: README.md (guided walkthrough), example app (Node + Python microservices) illustrating tool-binding adapters, a compact dev docker-compose for local index + runtime, telemetry presets (otel config + example dashboards), and a docs site entry that explains the pattern and trade-offs. Key design choices | - Unified tool matrix: a simple manifest-driven way to register tool adapters and map them to intent categories. - Split-index retrieval: example code shows how to query both an FAISS-like dense vector store for recent context and a SQLite-backed sparse inverted index for older archival docs, and how to merge/rank results. - Adaptive routing policy: a lightweight policy that favors dense index for low-latency user-facing queries and falls back to sparse for broad recall. - Telemetry probes: token-level sampling, tool-call spans, and a small set of example alerts for retrieval regressions. Checklist | - [x] Quickstart tutorial and README - [x] Example app (Node worker + Python retriever) - [x] Dev docker-compose and Makefile commands - [x] Docs site page and sidebar entry - [x] Unit tests for the retrieval merge and tool adapters - [x] Telemetry presets and sample dashboards Local test instructions | 1) cd quickstarts/unified-tool-matrix 2) make dev-up (starts local vector index, fake external tool stubs, and example runtime) 3) curl -X POST localhost:8080/ask -d '{"query":"summarize recent product notes and add action items to my calendar"}' 4) Open http://localhost:9411/trace to inspect spans and tool calls Notes on productionization | This quickstart intentionally keeps components small; for production we recommend pinning model versions, replacing the in-memory vector store with a managed store, and using Dedicated or Private deployment for the retriever worker. The README includes a migration checklist. Impact and testing | Added unit tests and an integration smoke CI job that runs the dev-compose and runs two sample workflows. Perf impact is zero on the main runtime; all new code is behind a quickstart-only directory and not shipped in the core runtime. Rollout and docs | Docs entry added under docs/quickstarts/unified-tool-matrix.md, and the site sidebar updated to include the new quickstart. Related | ENG-3321 (design), PM-114 (customer story), SUP-7789 (support follow-up).

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice thin scaffold — can we make the default dev compose use a smaller FAISS memory footprint? On my laptop it hit swap when running smoke CI. (requested change)
Asha Nair: Updated docker-compose to a low-memory vector store config and added a note in README about memory limits. Also added the --memory flag to the Makefile dev-up command. (author reply)
Sofia Martinez: Could you add a short example showing how to pin a model variant and how the quickstart demonstrates fallback routing? I want customers to see the migration path. (comment)
Asha Nair: Added a subsection in docs/quickstarts/unified-tool-matrix.md describing model pinning and a sample policy file. (author reply)
Jordan Patel: Tests look good, left one minor nit in test naming. Approving after that is fixed. (approved with minor change)
Asha Nair: Renamed the test and added a clarifying docstring. Pushed a small fixup. (author reply)
CI bot: integration-smoke re-run after compose memory fix — all checks passed. (automation)
Release lead (Sofia Martinez): Verified docs rendering in the staging site preview and confirmed the sidebar entry looks correct. (approval)
Merge: Squash-merged by Asha Nair after approvals. (merge note)
notes_for_reviewer: Focus on the retrieval merge strategy and telemetry spans — the adapters are intentionally minimal; we expect product teams to replace them with real connectors.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover merge heuristics and adapter fallbacks. Integration smoke brings up dev-compose and runs two end-to-end scenarios: (1) short-latency query hitting dense index, (2) broad recall query that merges dense + sparse results. CI re-run after memory fixes passed.
how_to_run_locally: cd quickstarts/unified-tool-matrix && make dev-up && curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8080/ask -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query":"what changed in the product notes this week and add a calendar event"}'
compatibility_notes: This quickstart targets Redwood API v1 and SDKs >= v0.7.0. The manifest format is intentionally stable but extensible. No breaking changes to core services.
